title: Caching, performance, and resilience in one screen
rememberThis: IMemoryCache = one pod; Redis IDistributedCache = whole farm — tenant id always in keys.
Cache stampede: GetOrCreateAsync or Redis lock when hot key expires — not 500 parallel DB hits.
Output cache before endpoint on anonymous GET; EvictByTag on writes; never cache user JSON without vary key.
Rate limit: sliding/token bucket beats fixed-window boundary burst; 429 with Retry-After.
Polly: retry GET 5xx, breaker fail-fast, timeout — no blind POST retry.
async all the way — .Result starves thread pool (queue-length high, CPU low).
Fix SQL index and N+1 before Redis — p95 proves the fix.
bullets: Onboarding slow API playbook: segment p95 by tenant → counters → trace → SQL vs pool vs cache.
dotnet-counters: threadpool-queue-length, current-requests, gc-heap-size, SQL connects.
EF: AsNoTracking + Select DTO + composite index (TenantId, CreatedAt) after bulk import.
AddStandardResilienceHandler on HttpClient; log circuit OnOpened.
UseRateLimiter early; partition by tenant_id not shared NAT IP for B2B APIs.
Hybrid L1 memory 30s + L2 Redis 5min for dashboard keys after large customer go-live.
